author: Karl Rock
description:
At first this market in Karachi, Pakistan, looks chaotic and dirty… then the people completely change the experience. Empress Market is one of the oldest and most famous markets in Karachi, Pakistan. Built in 1889 during British rule and named after Queen Victoria, it has been the commercial heart of Saddar for over a century. Today the market is packed with everything - spices, meat, pets, groceries, street food, and daily life happening all at once.

But Empress Market also has a complicated history. The site was originally a parade ground where freedom fighters were executed after the 1857 uprising, and over time the area developed a reputation for informal trade, overcrowding and crackdowns by city authorities. Despite that, locals here are incredibly welcoming and the market remains a place where people from every background come together.

In this vlog I walk through the chaos, meet the shopkeepers, and experience the real atmosphere of Karachi beyond the headlines.
